Analytic referenceReference for the same problem Lake at rest: wet and emerged equilibrium over represented bed q_i=0; h_i=max(eta0-z_i,0); z_i=cellmean(z); eta0=.5 or .1. Use g9.81,[0,25]m and200cells. Represent z=.2−.05(x−10)² on8<x<12 by split Gauss8 cell means, initializing h_i=max(eta0−z_i,0),q_i0 with eta0=.5/.1m. Hydrostatic reconstruction preserves equilibrium over this represented piecewise-constant bed; this differs from directly averaging depth over the continuous bed. Exact lake balance concerns the represented cell bed. Moving steady states retain finite-time numerical error. Transcritical flows, jumps, friction, rain, infiltration, 2D flow and fully discrete entropy stability are outside scope. Semi-analytic referenceReference for the same problem SWASHES steady flow: subcritical Bernoulli root q=4.42; h+z+q²/(2gh²)=2+q²/(8g); h>(q²/g)^(1/3). Use g9.81,[0,25]m, the parabolic bed, discharge q4.42m²/s and downstream depth2m. Independently bisect the subcritical root of h+z+q²/(2gh²)=2+q²/(8g) and qualify cell quadrature. PDE runs on100/200/400cells start from the steady reference and advance to t2; they do not reproduce the original rest-to-steady transient. Exact lake balance concerns the represented cell bed. Moving steady states retain finite-time numerical error. Transcritical flows, jumps, friction, rain, infiltration, 2D flow and fully discrete entropy stability are outside scope. Saved result / JSON Reference and validation details → Numerical methods Hydrostatic reconstruction, shared HLL flux and left/right pressure corrections discretize the bed source; forward Euler and face CFL .4. Lakes use reflecting walls. Moving subcritical boundaries impose upstream q and downstream h, extrapolating the other datum. No state floors, clipping or retries. Algebraically factor HLL updates into nonnegative water packets; advected momentum uses those same rounded masses, without a small-depth threshold or subsequent repair.
